title: Work Journal suggestions: the text gets its own full-width line, with pills and buttons underneath
story: Work Journal suggestions used to squeeze their text into a narrow strip beside their tags and buttons, so a long line wrapped to about a dozen short lines. Now the text reads across the whole suggestions box like a normal sentence, and the project and source tags and the Accept and Reject buttons sit on a line underneath. Nothing else about suggestions changed.

checks.criterion: Each suggestion's text sits alone on a full-width line; beneath it the project pill and source tag are on the left and Accept and Reject on the right, still clearly apart.
checks.steps: Start Maestro fresh and open a throwaway project called demo-shop. Open the Work Journal side panel at its narrow default width. Create today's page. Press 'run now', or wait for a suggestion with a long line such as '01:00 - Opened nine issues for the demo shop checkout and cart pages'.
checks.expected: The text wraps across the full width of the suggestions box, not in a thin column. Under it, the demo-shop pill and the source tag are on the left; the green tick and red cross are on the right, about a button's width apart. Accept adds the line to the page; Reject hides the suggestion. The 'next run · run now' footer and the box height are unchanged.
